chapter: Friars Inn, NORK and Chicago influences
title: How the two four-piece bands came together as the Rhythm Kings
summary: Steiner and Ashcraft recall the Chicago meetings and Erie Cafe jobs where Brunies, Pettis and the Snyders formed the group.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Frank Snyder tells me about their meeting, Brunus, over here on North Avenue in Halsted, where they'd come to Jim, finding some people that they could work with. And he said that's where he met Brunus long before they joined together to form the New Orleans Rhythm Kings.
I think Pettis told me that they played as two separate, that the two four-piece bands got together as an eight-piece band, often on Sundays.
And I think one or the other had been playing at the Erie Cafe.
Yes, Snyder. And Brunus and Merez had been playing with Rag Baby Stevens. Do you happen to know a drummer?
Yeah, I remember his name very well.

Down here on Madison Street, just about south of us, Madison and Halsted, or Madison and Ashland, in that neighborhood. Maybe Tommy Thomas' or some of the joints that were then popular in that area. That was a hot area.
